tree.question: Can you ping a public IP directly? (e.g. ping -c 2 8.8.8.8)

yes.question: Are you on a VPN or corporate network?

yes.cause: Your VPN may be overriding DNS settings or split-DNS is misconfigured.
fixes: Check VPN DNS settings — ensure split-DNS is configured correctly
Try: sudo resolvectl dns <interface> 8.8.8.8 8.8.4.4
Or add 'DNS=8.8.8.8' to /etc/systemd/resolved.conf and restart: sudo systemctl restart systemd-resolved

no.cause: Your configured nameserver is reachable on the network but not responding to DNS queries.
fixes: Try a different DNS server: sudo resolvectl dns <iface> 8.8.8.8
Edit /etc/resolv.conf: sudo nano /etc/resolv.conf — add 'nameserver 8.8.8.8'
Check if systemd-resolved is running: sudo systemctl status systemd-resolved
Restart resolved: sudo systemctl restart systemd-resolved

no.cause: Your DNS server IP is configured but not reachable — likely a network or DHCP issue.
fixes: Run: sudo dhclient -r && sudo dhclient to renew DHCP (may fix DNS assignment)
Temporarily override: sudo resolvectl dns <iface> 8.8.8.8 8.8.4.4
If using NetworkManager: nmcli dev show | grep DNS

no.cause: /etc/resolv.conf has no nameserver entries — DNS has nowhere to send queries.
fixes: Check symlink: ls -la /etc/resolv.conf (should point to systemd stub)
Re-link: sudo ln -sf /run/systemd/resolve/stub-resolv.conf /etc/resolv.conf
Or manually add: echo 'nameserver 8.8.8.8' | sudo tee /etc/resolv.conf
Restart networking: sudo systemctl restart systemd-networkd

no.question: Does 'ip route' show a default gateway?

yes.cause: A default route exists but traffic isn't reaching the internet. Likely a gateway, firewall, or interface problem.
fixes: Ping your gateway: ip route | grep default (get gateway IP, then ping it)
Check interface status: ip link show && ip addr show
Restart networking: sudo systemctl restart NetworkManager
Check for firewall rules: sudo iptables -L -n

no.cause: Your machine has no default gateway — it doesn't know how to reach the internet.
fixes: If using DHCP: sudo dhclient <interface>  (e.g. sudo dhclient eth0)
Manual route: sudo ip route add default via <gateway-ip>
Check if NetworkManager is running: sudo systemctl status NetworkManager
Restart NetworkManager: sudo systemctl restart NetworkManager

tree.question: Is this a 'Connection refused' or 'Connection timed out' error?

yes.question: Can you ping the target host?
Is SSH running on the remote host? (try: nc -zv <host> 22)
Is SSH running on a non-standard port?

yes.cause: The remote SSH daemon is listening on a port other than 22.
fixes: Connect specifying port: ssh -p <port> user@host
Check remote sshd config: sudo grep Port /etc/ssh/sshd_config
Add to ~/.ssh/config: Host <alias>\n  HostName <host>\n  Port <port>

no.diagnosis: SSH daemon not running or firewall blocking port 22
no.cause: Port 22 appears closed — sshd may be stopped or a firewall is dropping packets.
fixes: On remote (if accessible): sudo systemctl start sshd
Check firewall: sudo ufw status && sudo ufw allow ssh
Check iptables: sudo iptables -L -n | grep 22
Verify sshd is installed: sudo apt install openssh-server

no.cause: The host is reachable via ping (ICMP) but TCP connections are being blocked or the host is down.
fixes: Check if a firewall is blocking TCP: sudo ufw status
Try traceroute: traceroute <host>
Verify the IP/hostname is correct
Check if the host is a VM — ensure it's powered on and networking is bridged/NAT correctly

no.cause: Cannot reach the host at all — likely a network, VM, or IP misconfiguration.
fixes: Verify the hostname/IP is correct
Check the host is powered on
For VMs: check network adapter mode (bridged vs NAT) in your hypervisor
Check your routing: ip route show
Try from a different network to isolate the issue

no.question: Is the error 'Host key verification failed' or 'WARNING: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED'?

yes.cause: The remote host's key doesn't match what's stored in your known_hosts — this can be a legit key change (reinstall, new VM) or a MITM warning.
fixes: If you trust the host changed legitimately: ssh-keygen -R <hostname>
Then reconnect and accept the new key
Never blindly remove keys if this is a production server — verify the key fingerprint with the admin first

no.question: Is the error 'Permission denied (publickey)' or 'No supported authentication methods'?

yes.question: Are you using SSH key authentication (not password)?

yes.cause: Your public key isn't in the remote's authorized_keys, or key permissions are wrong.
fixes: Copy your key: ssh-copy-id user@host
Or manually: cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub | ssh user@host 'mkdir -p ~/.ssh && cat >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys'
Fix permissions on remote: chmod 700 ~/.ssh && chmod 600 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
Check SSH agent: ssh-add -l  (add key if missing: ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_rsa)
Debug with: ssh -vvv user@host

no.cause: The server only allows key-based auth, but you're attempting password login.
fixes: Generate a key pair: ssh-keygen -t ed25519
Copy to remote (if you have console access): ssh-copy-id user@host
Or ask the admin to add your public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
To enable password auth (not recommended for internet-facing): sudo nano /etc/ssh/sshd_config — set PasswordAuthentication yes, then sudo systemctl restart sshd

no.cause: The error doesn't match common patterns — verbose output will help identify the cause.
fixes: Run with verbose logging: ssh -vvv user@host
Check sshd logs on remote: sudo journalctl -u sshd -n 50
Verify sshd config is valid: sudo sshd -t

categories.name: APT Package Manager
categories.description: APT and dpkg package management errors

tree.question: Is the error related to a lock file? (e.g. 'Could not get lock /var/lib/dpkg/lock')

yes.question: Is another apt or dpkg process currently running? (check: ps aux | grep apt)

yes.cause: Another package manager process is running — wait for it to complete.
fixes: Wait for the other process to finish
If it's a stuck/zombie process: sudo kill <pid>
Then: sudo dpkg --configure -a

no.cause: A previous apt/dpkg run was interrupted and left behind a lock file.
fixes: Remove lock files: sudo rm /var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend && sudo rm /var/lib/dpkg/lock && sudo rm /var/cache/apt/archives/lock
Reconfigure dpkg: sudo dpkg --configure -a
Then retry your command

no.question: Is the error about fetching/downloading packages? (e.g. '404 Not Found', 'Unable to fetch', 'Hash Sum mismatch')

yes.question: Do you have working internet connectivity? (ping -c 2 8.8.8.8)

yes.diagnosis: Repository index stale or source unavailable
yes.cause: Package lists are outdated or the repository URL returned an error (404/mismatch).
fixes: Update package lists: sudo apt update
Clear apt cache: sudo apt clean && sudo apt update
Check for broken sources: sudo apt update 2>&1 | grep -i error
Remove failing third-party PPAs: sudo add-apt-repository --remove ppa:<name>
If a specific repo is broken: check /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ and disable the offending file

no.cause: apt cannot reach the repositories because the machine has no network connectivity.
fixes: Fix network first — run 'netreason diagnose' with a network error to troubleshoot
If you need to install offline: download .deb files on another machine and transfer via scp or USB
Use dpkg for offline installs: sudo dpkg -i <package>.deb

no.question: Is the error 'dpkg was interrupted' or about broken packages?

yes.cause: A previous install was interrupted, leaving the package database in a broken state.
fixes: Reconfigure pending packages: sudo dpkg --configure -a
Fix broken dependencies: sudo apt --fix-broken install
Force reinstall a specific package: sudo apt install --reinstall <package>
If still failing: sudo apt update && sudo apt dist-upgrade

no.cause: Unclassified apt issue — running update and fix-broken usually resolves most states.
fixes: Run: sudo apt update && sudo apt --fix-broken install
Check full error output for the specific package name
Try: sudo apt-get clean && sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get upgrade

categories.name: Network Connectivity
categories.description: General network connectivity and interface issues

tree.question: Does 'ip link show' show your network interface as UP?

yes.question: Does 'ip addr show' show an IP address on your main interface?
Can you ping your default gateway? (ip route | grep default, then ping <gateway>)

yes.cause: Your network connection is working fine — this is a DNS resolution problem.
fixes: Run 'netreason diagnose' and paste a DNS error for targeted help
Quick fix: sudo resolvectl dns <iface> 8.8.8.8 8.8.4.4
Or: echo 'nameserver 8.8.8.8' | sudo tee /etc/resolv.conf

no.cause: You can reach your local gateway but not the internet — firewall, NAT, or ISP issue.
fixes: Check firewall rules: sudo iptables -L -n && sudo ufw status
For VMs: verify NAT/bridged adapter is configured in the hypervisor
Check if proxy is required: env | grep -i proxy
Try: curl -v https://1.1.1.1 to test raw TCP to Cloudflare

no.cause: You have an IP but can't reach the gateway — wrong gateway, bad route, or physical/VM networking issue.
fixes: Verify gateway IP: ip route show default
Check interface is up: sudo ip link set <iface> up
For VMs: ensure the network adapter is connected in hypervisor settings
Try releasing and renewing DHCP: sudo dhclient -r <iface> && sudo dhclient <iface>
Restart NetworkManager: sudo systemctl restart NetworkManager

no.cause: Your network interface is up but has no IP — DHCP failed or static IP not configured.
fixes: Request DHCP lease: sudo dhclient <interface>  (e.g. eth0 or ens3)
Check DHCP client: sudo systemctl status isc-dhcp-client
For static IP (Netplan): sudo nano /etc/netplan/01-netcfg.yaml — add IP config, then: sudo netplan apply
Restart NetworkManager: sudo systemctl restart NetworkManager

no.question: Does the interface exist but show as DOWN?

yes.cause: The interface exists but is not active — it needs to be brought up.
fixes: Bring interface up: sudo ip link set <iface> up
For Netplan: sudo netplan apply
Check if NetworkManager manages it: nmcli dev status
Enable interface via NM: nmcli con up <connection-name>
For VMs: check the adapter is enabled in hypervisor settings

no.cause: No network interface is detected — driver issue, hardware problem, or wrong interface name.
fixes: List all interfaces: ip link show && lspci | grep -i net
Check for driver: dmesg | grep -i eth
For VMs: ensure a network adapter is added in hypervisor settings
Try loading driver: sudo modprobe e1000 (or relevant driver)
Check interface naming: ip link show (may be ens3, enp0s3, etc.)

categories.name: Systemd / Service
categories.description: Systemd service start failures and unit errors

tree.question: Is the error 'Unit not found' or 'No such file or directory'?

yes.question: Did you recently install the service package?

yes.cause: The package is installed but the systemd unit hasn't been enabled/loaded.
fixes: Reload systemd: sudo systemctl daemon-reload
Enable the service: sudo systemctl enable <service>
Then start it: sudo systemctl start <service>
Verify unit file exists: find /etc/systemd /lib/systemd -name '<service>.service'

no.cause: The service unit file doesn't exist — the package likely isn't installed.
fixes: Install the relevant package: sudo apt install <service-name>
Search for it: apt search <keyword>
If it's a custom service: create the unit file in /etc/systemd/system/<name>.service

yes.cause: The service has been explicitly masked (disabled at a deeper level than just disabled).
fixes: Unmask: sudo systemctl unmask <service>
Then enable and start: sudo systemctl enable --now <service>

no.question: Does the service start briefly then crash? (Active: failed, after activating)

yes.question: Is this a network-dependent service (nginx, mysql, etc.)?

yes.diagnosis: Service crashing on start — check logs for root cause
yes.cause: The service starts but its process exits immediately — config error, port conflict, or missing dependency.
fixes: Check detailed logs: sudo journalctl -u <service> -n 50 --no-pager
Check for port conflicts: sudo ss -tlnp | grep <port>
Validate config file (e.g. nginx): sudo nginx -t
Check for missing files/dirs referenced in config
Look at the ExecStart command: sudo systemctl cat <service>

no.cause: The service binary runs and exits — config, permissions, or dependency problem.
fixes: Read full logs: sudo journalctl -u <service> -xe
Check the ExecStart path exists: sudo systemctl cat <service>
Test running manually: sudo <binary-path> (to see raw error output)
Check permissions on required files/directories

no.cause: The service unit exists and isn't masked, but something is preventing activation.
fixes: Check full status: sudo systemctl status <service> -l
Read logs: sudo journalctl -u <service> --since '5 min ago'
Check dependencies: sudo systemctl list-dependencies <service>
Reload and retry: sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl start <service>

categories.name: Firewall / UFW
categories.description: UFW and iptables firewall configuration issues

tree.question: Are you trying to allow inbound connections to this machine?

yes.question: Is the specific port/service listed as ALLOW in ufw status?

yes.diagnosis: UFW rule exists — issue may be iptables or app config
yes.cause: UFW shows the rule, but traffic is still blocked — could be raw iptables rules or the app isn't binding to the right interface.
fixes: Check raw iptables: sudo iptables -L -n -v
Verify the app is listening: sudo ss -tlnp | grep <port>
Check if app binds to 0.0.0.0 or only localhost (127.0.0.1)
Temporarily disable UFW for testing: sudo ufw disable

no.cause: UFW is enabled and blocking the port — no allow rule exists for it.
fixes: Allow by service name: sudo ufw allow ssh  OR  sudo ufw allow http
Allow by port: sudo ufw allow <port>/tcp
Allow from specific IP: sudo ufw allow from <ip> to any port <port>
After adding rules: sudo ufw reload

no.cause: UFW is inactive, so it's not blocking anything. The issue is elsewhere.
fixes: Check raw iptables for rules: sudo iptables -L -n
Verify the service is running and listening: sudo ss -tlnp
Check application-level access control (e.g. AllowUsers in sshd_config)
Check if a cloud/host firewall (AWS Security Groups, etc.) is blocking traffic

no.question: Are you trying to make outbound connections that are being blocked?

yes.cause: Outbound connections are being filtered — rare on Ubuntu unless explicitly configured or on a corporate network.
fixes: Check UFW outbound rules: sudo ufw status verbose
UFW allows all outbound by default — check if policy was changed: sudo ufw default deny outgoing
To allow outbound: sudo ufw default allow outgoing
Check iptables OUTPUT chain: sudo iptables -L OUTPUT -n
Check if a corporate proxy is required: env | grep -i proxy

no.cause: Unclear firewall issue — reset and rebuild rules.
fixes: View all rules: sudo ufw status numbered
Reset to defaults (careful on remote servers): sudo ufw reset
Recommended baseline: sudo ufw default deny incoming && sudo ufw default allow outgoing && sudo ufw allow ssh && sudo ufw enable
